Based on these acute results, it would seem that sarcoplasmic proteins account for a considerable portion of aerobic-induced hypertrophic adaptations. Given evidence that the growth of a given muscle fiber is achieved at the expense of its aerobic endurance capacity (75), the accretion of mitochondrial proteins seems to have a negative impact on the ability to maximize gains in contractile proteins.
